videos.title: [One Million AI Engineer Special] How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco
videos.description:
[One Million AI Engineer Special] We’re celebrating one million subscribers on the AI Engineer YouTube channel with Mihail Eric, who teaches Stanford’s Modern Software Developer course and leads AI at Monaco.

What do you assign when students can finish last year’s homework with one prompt? For the second run of Stanford’s CS146S, Mihail Eric brought open-source maintainers into the course. Students have to understand an unfamiliar repo, propose a change, and explain it to the person who will review their code.

Mihail teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco. We work through his ten-week syllabus, from watching the tool calls inside Claude Code to deciding what a subagent should return to its parent. At Monaco, his team chose to build its own agent workspaces, buy code review tools, and give an on-call agent access to Datadog and GitHub. Mihail explains the reasoning behind those decisions.

Mihail thinks open-source repos will become agent-run software factories. If the factory can produce a patch, what should a junior engineer be learning to do?

AI Engineer CODE Summit — https://aie.codes
AI Engineer on YouTube — https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCLKPca3kwwd-B59HNr-_lvA

videos.title: GitHub’s Growth: 225M Developers, 34.3B Commits — Jay Parikh, EVP of CoreAI, Microsoft
videos.description:
GitHub’s next scaling challenge is the agent workload. The platform has 225 million developers and handled 34.3 billion commits over the past year. Jay Parikh, EVP of CoreAI at Microsoft, joins us straight after his GitHub Universe keynote to talk about rebuilding the software-development stack for that scale.

We get into Copilot Fusion’s approach to model orchestration and the quality–cost frontier; the harness underneath it; agents that carry a session across phone, desktop and VS Code; and the infrastructure work behind GitHub’s move to Azure. Jay also makes the case for measuring AI spending against completed work and business outcomes.

Along the way: why Jay skips pull requests in some of his own repos, Matt Pocock’s repo of Markdown instructions, and the open-source maintenance question behind replacing 2,000 dependencies with 20. Stay for the programmable conference badge at the end.

Before the interview: why agent traffic changes GitHub’s job, Jay’s infrastructure background, and AI Engineer CODE — Nov 10–12 in San Francisco. https://ai.engineer/code

Show notes
• GitHub’s 2026 Octoverse report — The original charts behind the 34.3B commits and agent-first PR figures. https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-commits-pushes-reach-new-highs-in-2026-as-developers-build-with-agents/
• Matt Pocock’s test-driven development skill — Open the Markdown file in the revision that was current when we recorded. https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/59db609eb1e18aaf59b63284d0e52255aff0c63c/skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md
• How Copilot Fusion routes a task — GitHub documents when a model drafts alone, when a judge reviews it, and when several models critique it. https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/models/copilot-fusion
• A Copilot session across clients — Watch GitHub’s original demos of a session continuing across devices and VS Code. https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-github-copilot-in-vs-code-universe-releases/
• Push protection for AI-detected secrets — The actual rejected push and what the developer sees in the terminal. https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-push-protection-beyond-predefined-secret-patterns/
• How GitHub migrates Git replicas — GitHub engineers show how they move live copies across data centers and Azure. https://github.blog/engineering/the-bridge-to-agent-scale-git-infrastructure/
• Copilot Automations cost controls — The launch example of per-run, daily, weekly and monthly AI credit limits. https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-new-tools-triggers-and-cost-controls-for-copilot-automations/
• The hackable Universe badge — Source, schematics and games for the badge that swyx holds up. https://github.com/badger/home

videos.title: Why Would Anthropic Go Public Now? — Jamin Ball, Altimeter
videos.description:
Will Anthropic make it from filing an S-1 to trading on Nasdaq? Jamin Ball, partner at Altimeter and author of Clouded Judgement, joins swyx to walk through the roadshow, the Thanksgiving window and what investors would need to believe about Claude.

Jamin makes a case for going public that starts with the lenders financing GPU clusters. Then he opens the accounts: in the first half of 2026, Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss and generated $3.9 billion in operating cash. He explains how the rising value of shares promised to early investors flows through the income statement, and why he watches the cost of serving Claude alongside revenue growth.

Recorded October 29, 2026. Jamin discusses his personal views and discloses Altimeter’s position in Anthropic.

videos.title: Cooking with Reducto’s CEO: Why PDFs Still Break AI — Adit Abraham
videos.description:
Why do PDFs still break AI? Reducto co-founder and CEO Adit Abraham joins Allen Park on Latent Space Cooking to talk AI document parsing and make a steak sandwich with burrata, torched peaches, and chimichurri.

From the YC pivot out of long-term memory to Reducto R1 and Deep Extract, Adit explains why even frontier models can miss rows in long documents, how his team catches failures in production, and what it takes to go from reading a PDF to reliably editing one. He also revisits the viral steak tweet that brought him into the kitchen.

Sponsorship and business inquiries: business@latent.space

We talk about:
• Why complex tables, handwriting, and unusual layouts still trip up AI
• When specialized models and extraction pipelines beat a general-purpose model
• Why 99% accuracy can still fall short, and where citations and human review help
• What independent benchmarks and production evals reveal about messy documents
• What changes at a billion pages a month, the scale Adit shared at filming
• What Reducto looks for in engineers, and why it lets candidates use AI in interviews
• What a Claude Code moment for office work might look like
